root_scope: Rational Hodge Conjecture for smooth projective complex varieties; no integral/generalized/Tate substitution.
problem_signature: After H4d1b normalized complete first-order obstruction vanishing to tangent surjectivity for a fixed chosen witness, determine whether fixed-witness tangent surjectivity is actually necessary for class propagation, or whether a class-constrained unmarked incidence image can dominate the Hodge branch while witnesses switch.

frozen_objects.class: flat rational alpha, type (p,p) along fixed irreducible local Hodge branch T through s0
frozen_objects.central_witness: one finite signed rational witness z0 for alpha at s0, with coefficient vector preserved only on the marked route
frozen_objects.marked_incidence: pi_marked: W_{alpha,z0}->T, local branch through z0
frozen_objects.unmarked_incidence: pi_unmarked: W_alpha^class->T, union/stack/local finite collection of coefficient-safe witness components constrained to realize alpha

success_contract: MARKED route: prove d pi_marked at z0 is onto T_s0 T, then separately higher-order/formal/algebraization/global continuation.

UNMARKED route: prove a class-constrained incidence image contains the relevant Hodge-branch germ (or another source-bound statement that yields an algebraic representative of alpha_s at each nearby s), without silently asserting deformation of z0.
For rational signed cycles, the unmarked incidence must retain a finite coefficient-safe witness category or otherwise prove exact equality of the realized rational class to alpha_s.
No first-order image/dimension statement may be promoted to all-order lifting without a fresh higher-order check.
adversarial_controls: Map A1->A1, x↦x^2: image is all of A1 over C, but d pi_0=0; unpointed image dominance does not imply marked tangent surjectivity.
Disjoint-union incidence: one rigid marked point over s0 plus a different component dominating T; existence of some nearby witness does not deform the chosen z0.
Nonreduced Hodge loci: tangent agreement can fail to control higher-order branch structure.
Witness switching can lose the exact rational class unless class/coefficient constraints are built into the incidence object.

solved_or_nearsolved_controls.source: Remke Kloosterman, arXiv:2104.14845v2 (2021), Theorem 4.14 and Proposition 3.2
solved_or_nearsolved_controls.usable_fact: For complete-intersection cycles in smooth hypersurfaces in projective space, the local Hodge locus is smooth and its irreducible component coincides with the unpointed locus of hypersurfaces containing a complete intersection of the fixed multidegree.
solved_or_nearsolved_controls.disanalogy: The theorem identifies a geometric image locus; it does not state that the originally marked Z deforms along every Hodge direction. Its flag-Hilbert proof contains additional tangent/fiber information but the marked surjectivity implication requires a separate pointwise smoothness/rank audit.

solved_or_nearsolved_controls.source: Bruzzo–Montoya, European J. Math. 9 (2023) 108, Theorem 5.4; arXiv:2203.00664 provenance
solved_or_nearsolved_controls.usable_fact: Under Macaulay-type and degree hypotheses, the local Noether-Lefschetz locus is an irreducible component of the projection of a flag Hilbert scheme, and the Hodge class deforms algebraically iff it remains Hodge.
solved_or_nearsolved_controls.disanalogy: This is a class-existence/unpointed incidence statement in a special toric setting, not a general smooth-projective fixed-witness deformation theorem.
